Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates bilateral pulmonary nodules and prominent hilar regions, which correspond to the bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and nodular opacities seen on the CT scan (Figure 1a). This combination of findings, particularly the "sarcoid galaxy sign" (conglomerate nodules surrounding a central mass-like lesion) visible on CT, is highly characteristic of sarcoidosis.
